company.name: Northpeak Realty
company.summary: Northpeak Realty is a residential real estate agency in Denver with 22 people. You help buyers and sellers with property listings, buyer inquiries, viewings, and offer paperwork. Your team uses a CRM, Zillow feeds, and DocuSign to run day to day work.
company.customers: Home buyers and sellers in Denver and nearby suburbs

roles.title: Real Estate Agent
repetitive_tasks: Answer inbound buyer calls and emails
Write and update property listing text
Log client notes and next steps in CRM

roles.title: Listing Coordinator
repetitive_tasks: Enter listing data into MLS and Zillow

roles.title: Buyer Inquiry Coordinator
repetitive_tasks: Respond to Zillow and website leads

strategy.situation: Northpeak Realty runs a 22 person residential agency in Denver with sales, transaction coordination, marketing, admin, and client services using CRM, Zillow feeds, DocuSign, and MLS. Leads, showings, and paperwork move through email, phone, and calendar work that the team manages manually.
strategy.complication: As lead volume and deal activity rise, response times and deadlines depend on people checking inboxes, calendars, and signature status by hand. That creates lost buyer opportunities, missed paperwork dates, and CRM records that fall behind.
strategy.governing_thought: Start with a lead response agent, a showing scheduler, and a transaction deadline chaser; they cut response delays, booking friction, and missed paperwork while your team stays in control.

key_arguments.headline: Inbound leads, showings, and transaction paperwork carry most repetitive work
key_arguments.support: Sales agents and the buyer inquiry coordinator spend their days answering leads, booking showings, and updating the CRM. Transaction coordinators chase signatures, deadlines, and missing fields across DocuSign and email. Marketing and admin handle steady copy, scheduling, and filing work that repeats every week.

key_arguments.headline: Lead response, showing scheduling, and deadline chasing are the best first agents
key_arguments.support: These three sit on high volume, rules based tasks that use systems you already have: CRM, Zillow feeds, calendar, and DocuSign. Each can be tested in weeks with clear quality checks. They reduce buyer wait times and missed dates without changing how agents sell.

key_arguments.headline: Launch with human review, measure errors, then expand to other departments
key_arguments.support: Phase one keeps a person approving messages, bookings, and deadline notices while the agent drafts and tracks. You review response times, error rates, and hours saved weekly, then move proven agents to listing, marketing, and admin work. Scale remains controlled because the same review model applies to each new agent.

strategy.executive_summary: Northpeak Realty runs a 22 person residential agency in Denver with sales, transaction coordination, marketing, admin, and client services using CRM, Zillow feeds, DocuSign, and MLS. maturity.label: Early automation
maturity.note: Northpeak Realty uses core real estate systems but relies on manual email, calendar, and CRM updates. There are no AI agents or automations in place today.

roadmap.title: Prove value with lead response, showing scheduling, and deadline chasing
items: Set up lead response agent with approved questions and CRM fields
Connect showing scheduler to agent calendars and CRM
Build transaction checklist templates and DocuSign reminder rules
Run daily human review for messages, bookings, and deadline notices
Track first response time, showing confirmations, and missed deadlines

roadmap.title: Extend proven agents to listing publishing, copy, and offer packets
items: Connect listing intake to MLS and Zillow field drafts
Add marketing copy agent with brand and fair housing review
Add offer packet assembly agent with field checks
Train listing and marketing staff on review and approval steps
Compare error rates and hours saved against phase one

roadmap.title: Add admin routing, CRM updates, and seller reporting
items: Deploy phone and viewing request agent at front desk
Add CRM note and follow up agent for sales team
Add weekly seller update agent for listing agents
Set escalation rules for legal, pricing, and contract questions
Review all agents monthly and retire any that do not meet targets

risks.risk: Automated replies may give wrong property or pricing information
risks.mitigation: Use approved answer libraries, keep humans approving first responses for two weeks, and route pricing or legal questions to an agent.

risks.risk: Agents may not trust or use the new workflows
risks.mitigation: Start with volunteers, show time saved in weekly reports, and keep agents in control of all client negotiations.

risks.risk: MLS, Zillow, and DocuSign rules may restrict automated actions
risks.mitigation: Follow each system's terms, limit access to approved accounts, and keep final submission or signature requests under human review.

risks.risk: CRM data may be incomplete or inconsistent
risks.mitigation: Define required fields, run weekly exception reports, and have the transaction coordinator fix gaps.
Use plain templates with agent names, allow quick edits, and keep personal notes for offers, negotiations, and sensitive updates.
